wstep: There is no recipe here for drying parasol mushroom caps.

ostrzezenia.tekst: The most frequent and most dangerous mushroom poisonings in Poland are caused by the death cap, which is mistaken for edible species such as the parasol mushroom.
Drying and cooking do not destroy the toxins of poisonous mushrooms, and only an expert can tell edible species from poisonous ones.

In Poland: if in doubt whether mushrooms are edible, take them fresh, before drying, to a sanitary-epidemiological station (sanepid); mushroom experts or classifiers there assess free of charge whether they are edible, inedible or poisonous.

akapity: Only mushrooms that are certainly safe to eat are dried; anyone who is not an expert in mushroom identification should preserve only commercially sold mushrooms.
Whole fruiting bodies, with cap and stem, are brought for assessment, because important identifying features are also on the stem; dried caps alone have no stem.
In Poland, a mushroom expert (grzyboznawca) is authorised to assess whether fresh and dried mushrooms are fit to eat.
Outside Poland this card does not name an institution that assesses mushrooms: if you are not sure a mushroom is edible, do not dry or eat it.

With the most dangerous mushrooms, such as the death cap, the first symptoms often appear long after eating, sometimes only after several days, and after a temporary improvement the condition can worsen rapidly; with symptoms of poisoning, call a doctor at once or go to hospital, and seek help also for people who ate the same dish even if they have no symptoms yet.
